title: Scoring Hawkins's 'Body and Soul' for Charlie Johnson: a dating argument
summary: Waters says he scored Trumbauer's solo and Hawkins's 'Body and Soul' for Charlie Johnson's band. Schaap shows the record postdates the band's heyday, so Waters says the band returned to Small's about 1940.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah, there were things like that. I took that number and made in three-part saxophones for Charlie Johnson.
You scored the solo?
Scored the solo, then harmonized it. And I did the same thing for "Body And Soul", Coleman Hawkins from the [ ] -
That was a decade later -
About, yeah, yeah.
What band did you score the "Body And Soul" Hawkins for?
Charlie Johnson's band.
No, you didn't.
Sure I did, sure I did.
Well, how would that be possible?
Well, I mean, I made that from a record, I know I made it. I -

I'll explain why I say how could that possibly have happened. You see, Coleman Hawkins made his "Body And Soul" on October 11th of '39, it came out at the earliest in mid-fall of '39, and the Charlie Johnson band was a thing of the past by this time -
Naaah, no. No, no, Charlie Johnson's band came to the Paradise in the late '20's -
That's what I just said -
and then had a recess of 3 - 2, 3 years and went back later on.
But it wasn't around in 1940 -
In '40, yeah. -
around '35 or '38 or something like that, that was the second time. He went there
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82

twice. That's the, he didn't work 10 years all at once, it was a pause between. Charlie, the band left Small's Paradise and went back, a lot of people don't know that. And that's a time that it was right in, not only did we do, make arrangement on "Body And Soul", Ben Whitted made arrangement on "Ding Dong Daddy" of Louie Armstrong and all that stuff.
I think -
You know what I mean, "Ding Dong Daddy" -
I think "Ding Dong Daddy" is 1931, that makes sense.
Yeah.
"Singin' The Blues" is 1927, that makes sense.
Yeah.
But you're trying to tell me that Charlie Johnson's Orchestra with people like Ben Whitted and yourself in it was still playing at Small's Paradise -
Not Ben Whitted, though, no, Ben Whitted wasn't there.
Well, who was there?
Coleman Hawkins wasn't - when I made this, when I made the solo, we got, we copied from the record.
Right, but what -
See?
band played it?
Charlie Johnson's band.
Charlie Johnson's was playing Small's Paradise in 1940?
1938, '9, around -
Well, the record is recorded October 11th, '39, you could not possibly have heard it one day earlier than that.
Well, I tell you, I mean I say, here's what you're confusing. How long do you think that Charlie Johnson stayed at Small's Paradise, what years -
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Even if he stayed there, if it stayed there 15 years, you said 10, it still wouldn't be enough.

Yeah, but I mean, but I mean I, it stayed there from the '20's, late '20's, for about 5 years, then went back after a 3 or 4 year period and stayed there again for 2 or 3 years. That's where that came in.
'Kay, well, I mean I'll look it when I get -
See, that's where you're look-, that's what you're not checkin' on -
No, I'm totally aware, I am checking on it -
We didn't stay right there all that time, you know, see. We left and then went back.
I understand, I understand, you told me -
And that was when - was it Coleman, Coleman Hawkins deal -
All I'm tryin' to say, I'm not trying to contradict you, I'm trying to say if Charlie Johnson's band played Coleman Hawkins's 'Body And Soul' solo -
I arranged it myself -
as arranged by Benny Waters, then Charlie Johnson's band had to have played Small's Paradise in 1940.
Well, that's it then, it was 1940 then.
Because it couldn't have been earlier -
That's all I'm saying. I'm not saying something did or didn't happen, I'm just saying what would have to happen to make what you're saying possible.
Yeah. Well, I mean, that's possible, see, that we stayed there into 1940 -
Uh huh -
it's possible.
